newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - Washington Post business - March 12.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Washington Post business - March 12.

text.p: The Washington Post carried the following stories on the front page of its business section on March 12:
WASHINGTON - Two privately held companies offered a plan requiring a break from the FCC to settle a turf war over the use of radio frequencies to offer telephone and Internet services over the air.
WASHINGTON - President Clinton wants TV broadcasters to donate air time for a massive government-run anti-drug campaign.

WASHINGTON - The Federal Trade Commission's decision to block Staples Inc.'s proposed acquisition of Office Depot Inc. appears only to enhance Staples' competitive position in the office products industry.

NEW YORK - The U.S. attorney in Brooklyn may have the first case of a broker who is charged not only with accepting a $100,000 bribe to sell worthless stock but also of allegedly saying he would kill employees who refused to lie for him.
WASHINGTON - As passenger train deficits burgeoned in the 1960s, railroads began attaching freight cars to some trains in an effort to hold down losses. Now, history may be repeating itself.
